about: One entry for every job-posting platform SLED JOBS reads or meets: every reader in ats.FETCHERS (html, the page scan, among them), the platforms researched live on 2026-11-19..21 that have no reader, and every vendor the finder's ELSEWHERE list recognises. Each entry says how a company's site shows the platform, how it publishes its postings, what robots.txt allows, where a board names its employer, its quirks, and which functions read and probe it.

Written from the code (the readers in scripts/ats.py, the finder's patterns in scripts/find_site_boards.py, the probes in scripts/verify_boards.py, build_board.board_url) and from the research of 2026-11-19..21, whose evidence sat in scratch files that are not kept. Where the research and the code disagree, the code is what runs, and the entry's notes say so. Nothing is guessed: what the sources do not settle says unknown.

How a platform is met. find_site_boards.py reads a company's own website: an address in one of its board patterns is a candidate, naming a board a reader takes; an address on a platform nothing reads, or a form of one we read that names no board, is tallied under elsewhere (ELSEWHERE, with TENANT_FORMS and _NO_BOARD_IN_IT saying which forms belong to which platform). The reader in ats.FETCHERS reads the board. verify_boards.board_says asks the board whose it is, and proven() decides whether the name it states is the company's. wire_found.py wires a found board only when both checks agree (the owner's rule, 2026-11-18).

measured_on lists the days the code or the research records a live measurement; a window (day..day) is a day within it that the research does not narrow down; unknown is none recorded. A form is a finder vendor id that belongs to the platform and names no board the wiring door can use.

statuses.read: A reader exists in ats.FETCHERS; the nightly crawl reads boards of this type.
statuses.build: Researched; worth a reader; not built yet.
statuses.maybe: Researched; worth a reader only on the conditions the entry names.
statuses.skip: Researched; cannot or should not be read, for the reason the entry gives.
statuses.seen: The finder recognises it (find_site_boards.ELSEWHERE); not researched yet.

adp.name: ADP Workforce Now
adp.spot: The careers page a person opens, workforcenow.adp.com/mascsr/default/mdf/recruitment/recruitment.html?cid=<uuid>[&ccId=<n>_<n>], or the API address that page calls (find_site_boards' own patterns). The cid is the ref, followed by '|<ccId>' only when the link names a career centre other than ADP's default. Hint: workforcenow.adp.com. Nothing guesses a cid: it comes from a link the company published.

forms.adp-other: An address on workforcenow, myjobs or recruiting.adp.com that names no cid.

adp.publishes: A public JSON API, one GET: https://workforcenow.adp.com/mascsr/default/careercenter/public/events/staffing/v1/job-requisitions?cid=<cid>&ccId=<ccId>&lang=en_US&locale=en_US -> jobRequisitions[] with requisitionTitle, requisitionLocations[].nameCode.shortName, itemID and postDate. The careers page itself is a ~5 KB shell that draws nothing until its script asks that API. The reader makes one request and does not page.
adp.link: None of its own: board_url links the company's website.
adp.robots: Not asked by the reader: it reads ADP's JSON API through ats._get, which the owner's ruling of 2026-10-09 exempts as an interface published for programs. Not measured.
adp.employer: No identity probe: verify_boards.board_says answers 'no identity probe written for adp', so no ADP board can pass proven().
quirks: Verified 2026-09-02 against Zenner USA (11 requisitions), with a cid read off the company's own careers page.
Most portals answer on ADP's default ccId (19000101_000001); the few that need another carry it in the ref.
The location is ADP's label, a site name then a place ('Minol - Addison, TX'), and the reader keeps the place. The address block beside it was empty on every row seen.

discover_ats.MARKERS still files the recruitment.html address as type html, which reads as a JavaScript shell ('page too small'); ten companies sat in the discovery log that way when the reader was written.

applicantpro.name: ApplicantPro (isolved)
applicantpro.spot: <label>.applicantpro.com or <label>.isolvedhire.com (one platform on two root domains, run by isolved) in an href, a src, an iframe or frame, or a redirect (find_site_boards; 'www' and the vendor's own labels skipped). The whole tenant host is the ref: the label alone does not say which domain, and it is not the company's name ('casellejobs'). Hints: applicantpro.com, isolvedhire.com.

forms.applicantpro-other: An address on applicantpro.com or isolvedhire.com that names no tenant: the 'Powered by ApplicantPro' link, and the www.applicantpro.com/openings/<label>/... form a board's own og:url uses, whose label the finder does not read.

applicantpro.publishes: Two requests a board. The /jobs/ page (https://<host>/jobs/) names the domain id the list is asked by, in its JobListings componentData (domainId and getParams), and the list is the call that component makes: GET https://<host>/core/jobs/<domainId>?getParams=<the page's getParams, as JSON> -> {success: true, data: {jobs: [...], jobCount}}, each job with title, city, abbreviation (the state), iso3, jobUrl, startDateRef ('Nov 17, 2026'), workplaceType, payType, minSalary, maxSalary, payTypeFrame and payDetails. The ad is each posting's schema.org block (one request a posting, behind FETCH_DETAILS). No paging: jobCount equalled the rows on every board read.
applicantpro.robots: Asked at every hop: read as pages, held to the tenant's host. Measured 2026-11-19..21: every tenant host read, on both root domains, allows /jobs/, /core/jobs/ and the posting pages, and disallows only /admin/, /stats/ and the internal-jobs paths. Genasys's host gave no rules, and its site is disabled.
applicantpro.employer: The feed names nobody. The /jobs/ page's courierCurrentRouteData states two names: career_site_name, the site the employer set up, and organization_name, the ApplicantPro account behind it. verify_boards._applicantpro states both and requires the site's own name, so a sister brand's site on another company's account states two names and goes to the owner's queue: Black Mountain Software's board is on Caselle's account (2026-11-19).
quirks: A DISABLED SITE ANSWERS 200: Genasys's /jobs/ lands, on the same host, on /notset.php?...&disabled=1, 'This career site has been disabled'. That is a board that is gone, never one with nothing open.

min..max is pay only on a 'Salary' or 'Hourly' row whose payDetails names no commission, OTE, bonus or equity: on 'Base + Commission' it runs from the base floor to the OTE ceiling (LYT's Senior AE: 82000-248000 against a stated base of $82k-$124k). The posting page's baseSalary is not taken either, so a figure refused here cannot come back by another door.

The list call is the board's own front-end endpoint, not a published API, and its bundles are hash-named, so a front-end release can change it. The research found a server-rendered fallback list at /iframe/mobile; the code does not read it.
startDateRef is read as '%b %d, %Y' (posted_date does not take that form); a city of 'Remote' is a way of working, not a place.
discover_ats.MARKERS still files <label>.applicantpro.com and <label>.isolvedhire.com as type html.
notes: The research left it to the owner whether the probe states organization_name beside career_site_name (stating both sends Black Mountain to his queue); the code states both. The code is what runs.

ashby.name: Ashby
ashby.spot: jobs.ashbyhq.com/<slug>, its embed form jobs.ashbyhq.com/embed?org=<slug>, or the API address api.ashbyhq.com/posting-api/job-board/<slug> (find_boards.PATTERNS and discover_ats.MARKERS, borrowed by find_site_boards), plus the finder's own form for a board whose name has a space in it, which arrives as %20 and is read whole ('flock safety', not 'flock'). Hint: ashbyhq.com. The slug is kept as the page spelt it.
ashby.publishes: A documented JSON API, one GET for the whole board: https://api.ashbyhq.com/posting-api/job-board/<slug>?includeCompensation=true -> {jobs: [...]}, each with title, location, jobUrl or applyUrl, descriptionPlain, publishedAt, workplaceType and, with includeCompensation, pay as numbers: the only board here that publishes a pay range as numbers on its list endpoint. No paging.
ashby.robots: Not asked by the reader: it reads Ashby's documented feed through ats._get (exempt under the owner's ruling of 2026-10-09). The identity probe reads the board's own page, jobs.ashbyhq.com/<slug>, through verify_boards._board_page, robots.txt asked at every hop. What either host's robots.txt says is not recorded.
ashby.employer: The feed names nobody ({jobs, apiVersion}). The board's own page assigns window.__appData, whose organization block carries the display name and the website the employer gave Ashby: verify_boards.board_says reads the feed, then _ashby_page states organization.name and gives publicWebsite as the site proven() holds to the one on file. A board marked isDemoOrg names nobody. The slug (hostedJobsPageSlug) is never a name: 'snd' is Social News Desk.
quirks: workplaceType gives the mode; isRemote is deliberately unused, because False means not remote, not onsite.

bamboohr.name: BambooHR
bamboohr.spot: <slug>.bamboohr.com (find_boards.PATTERNS and discover_ats.MARKERS, borrowed by find_site_boards); the slug is lowered. Hint: bamboohr.com.
bamboohr.publishes: JSON, one GET: https://<slug>.bamboohr.com/careers/list -> {result: [...], meta}, each opening with jobOpeningName, atsLocation and location parts, and id. The list carries no description: /careers/<id>/detail carries the description and a compensation field (one request a posting, behind FETCH_DETAILS). No paging.
bamboohr.robots: Not asked by the reader (ats._get, exempt under the owner's ruling of 2026-10-09). The identity probe reads the careers page through verify_boards._board_page, robots.txt at every hop. Not measured.
bamboohr.employer: The list names nobody. The careers page states the name in og:site_name, and NOT in its <title>, which is the bare word 'BambooHR' on every board: verify_boards._bamboohr reads the list for the count, then _bamboohr_page.
quirks: atsLocation is read first: location is {city: null, state: null} on every row of every board checked, while atsLocation holds 'Denver, Colorado, United States' one key over.
compensation on the detail record was null on every sample on file.
BambooHR's marketing site is www.bamboohr.com, on the domain its tenants' boards sit under, so the probe holds every hop to the board's own host.

breezy.name: Breezy HR
breezy.spot: <slug>.breezy.hr (find_boards.PATTERNS and discover_ats.MARKERS, borrowed by find_site_boards); the slug is lowered. Hint: breezy.hr.
breezy.publishes: JSON, one GET: https://<slug>.breezy.hr/json -> a list of positions with name, location.name, url, published_date and pay as text in the list ('$160,000 - $200,000 / year'). The description is only on each posting page's schema.org JobPosting (one request a posting, behind FETCH_DETAILS). No paging.
breezy.robots: Not asked for the feed (ats._get, exempt under the owner's ruling of 2026-10-09). The posting pages behind FETCH_DETAILS and the probe's fallback page are read as pages, robots.txt at every hop. Not measured.
breezy.employer: Stated in the feed: company.name on every position, never company.friendly_id, which repeats the slug ('vetro-fibermap-inc' where the name is 'VETRO, Inc'). An empty feed ('[]', Polco's) names nobody, so verify_boards._breezy falls back to the hosted page's breezy-doc-title meta (_breezy_page); not its og:title, which is a slogan the employer types ('Join Our Team').
quirks: Pay is free in the list; only the description costs a request.

comeet.name: Comeet (Spark Hire Recruit)
comeet.spot: The company's own iframe or API call, which hands its browser the company uid and the public token together (comeet.co/jobs/<UID>/social?token=..., or .../jobs/<UID>/<position UID>/apply?token=..., or comeet.co/careers-api/2.0/company/<UID>/positions?token=...); a COMEET.init({...}) script, read one key at a time because Cognyte's object is not JSON; or a hosted board, www.comeet.com/jobs/<slug>/<UID> (find_site_boards). A uid is two hex digits, a dot and three more ('F2.004'). The ref is '<UID>|<TOKEN>' as the company's page gave them, or the hosted board's address. Hint: comeet.

forms.comeet-other: Any other comeet.co or comeet.com address (a terms link on support.comeet.co, a plugin page).
forms.comeet-tenant: A Comeet address naming a company uid with no token to read it by: a doubt beside a board, unless it names the very tenant a board on the page already is.

comeet.publishes: Comeet's careers API, one request a company, the ad on &details=true: GET https://www.comeet.co/careers-api/2.0/company/<UID>/positions?token=<TOKEN>&details=true -> an array of positions with name, location (name, city, state, country), workplace_type, url_comeet_hosted_page and details[] (Description, Responsibilities, Requirements, in order). For a hosted-board ref the reader first reads the hosted page's COMPANY_DATA for the token: two requests. No paging.
comeet.link: A hosted-board ref is linked as it is; a '<UID>|<TOKEN>' ref has no page of its own a person can open, the pair is never printed, and board_url links the company's website.
comeet.robots: Asked at every hop: read as pages, held to the host. Measured 2026-11-19..21: www.comeet.co and www.comeet.com serve the same file, which allows the API, the iframe and the hosted pages and disallows ?src= and utm_ parameters (among a few others); never add them.
comeet.employer: Stated on every position: company_name. A hosted board's page also states the account's name and the website it gave (COMPANY_DATA.name and website), both held to the record (verify_boards._comeet). An empty list names nobody unless the board is a hosted page, which still names itself. The page <title> is the vendor's ('Spark Hire Recruit Jobs | ...') and is never read.
quirks: Never read: the referral bounty (company_referrals_reward, '3000$', is not pay), the apply alias (email), the categories (one named a hiring manager), and location.is_remote, which is true on every Hybrid row.
No posting date: time_updated is an edit stamp, so posted is None.
The token is the public one the company's careers page gives every visitor's browser; a stored one stops working if the employer issues a new one.
WordPress 'Comeet Jobs' plugin sites (Cellebrite's) keep the token on the server and print no uid, token or comeet address: nothing can be lifted from them, and no slug or uid is ever guessed.
Mostly a platform for Israeli companies: 26 of the 105 rows the research read were US-located.
The vendor now calls itself Spark Hire Recruit; the hosts are unchanged, and a move to new hosts would break the reader and the finder's patterns.
notes: The research said an empty feed needs a fallback to the hosted page, as breezy's probe has; the code names a board through its hosted page only when the ref is that page, so an empty board on file as '<UID>|<TOKEN>' names nobody. The code is what runs.

gem.name: Gem
gem.spot: jobs.gem.com/<slug> (find_site_boards). The slug is never derived from the company id: City Detect's is citydetect. Hint: jobs.gem.com.
gem.publishes: Every jobs.gem.com page, board and job alike, is the same ~4 KB JavaScript shell with no JobPosting JSON-LD. The shell calls one public GraphQL endpoint that needs no auth, key or Referer: POST https://jobs.gem.com/api/public/graphql/batch, operation JobBoardList, which the reader sends with descriptionHtml added to the board's own query (and once more without it if that field errors). One request.
gem.robots: Not asked: a POST (ats._post_json). Not measured.
gem.employer: Stated by the board's own API, in the one call the reader makes: jobBoardExternal.teamDisplayName (verify_boards._gem). A slug that does not exist answers jobBoardExternal null and names nobody.
quirks: THE DISCRIMINATOR IS jobBoardExternal: a live board with nothing open and a slug that does not exist return a byte-identical empty postings list, and only the board object tells them apart, so a missing board is Unknown, never None found.
locations[].name never reaches a row: Gem prints team labels there ('City Detect (AL)'), which would read as an Alabama desk.

greenhouse.name: Greenhouse
greenhouse.spot: boards.greenhouse.io/<slug> or job-boards.greenhouse.io/<slug>, the embed greenhouse.io/embed/job_board[/js]?for=<slug> and the feed boards-api.greenhouse.io/v1/boards/<slug> (find_boards.PATTERNS and discover_ats.MARKERS, borrowed by find_site_boards), plus the finder's own forms: the application-form embed greenhouse.io/embed/job_app?for=<slug> and the older api.greenhouse.io/v1/boards/<slug>. Hint: greenhouse.io.

forms.greenhouse-eu: A board in Greenhouse's European region (job-boards.eu.greenhouse.io/<x>). fetch_greenhouse asks the American API only, so it is tallied apart until a reader can ask the European host: handed over as an ordinary ref it would be asked where it does not live, a 404 or another employer's board.
forms.greenhouse-shortlink: A grnh.se short link, which names no board; a redirect that lands on one is walked one hop further, because Greenhouse's next hop is usually the board.

greenhouse.publishes: A documented JSON API, one GET: https://boards-api.greenhouse.io/v1/boards/<slug>/jobs?content=true -> {jobs: [...]} with title, location.name, absolute_url, content (the ad, in the same request), first_published and pay_input_ranges. No paging.
greenhouse.robots: Not asked: a documented feed read through ats._get (exempt under the owner's ruling of 2026-10-09); the probe reads the same feed. Not measured.
greenhouse.employer: Stated in the feed: company_name on every job. verify_boards.board_says keeps every distinct name (a parent's hub stamps different names on different jobs) and the apply hosts of the first eight. judge() still reads it with the older substring test, under which a parent passes ('Jacobs' for 'StreetLight Data (Jacobs)'); proven() requires every name to equal the record's.
quirks: posted is first_published, never updated_at, which moves on any edit.
Pay is in cents on some payloads (min_cents, max_cents) and in units on others (min_value, max_value); both are read and neither is assumed.
Many companies share boards-api.greenhouse.io, so ats' per-host gate holds them HOST_PAUSE (0.5 s) apart.

gusto.name: Gusto
gusto.spot: jobs.gusto.com/boards/<name>-<uuid> (find_site_boards). The segment is never derived from the company id: kaiden-ai's board is kaiden-incorporated-<uuid>. Hint: jobs.gusto.com.

forms.gusto-posting: A jobs.gusto.com/postings/... link to one job, which names no board; a redirect that lands on one is walked one hop further.

gusto.publishes: Server-rendered HTML with no API, no JSON-LD and no embedded payload: https://jobs.gusto.com/boards/<segment>, read in five states, each with a positive marker: populated (/postings/ links), empty ('There are no open positions currently', on a page titled 'Careers at X'), closed ('This job board is closed.'), gone (the body says 404) and anything else (Unknown). A paginated board raises rather than report part of itself.
gusto.robots: Asked at every hop (ats._page). Not measured.
gusto.employer: Only the title pattern 'Careers at X', believed when the page's first heading says the same X (verify_boards._gusto). A closed board is titled the bare word 'Careers' and names nobody; the ref's own name segment is never read.
quirks: CLOSED IS NOT EMPTY: a closed board means the employer moved (City Detect left Gusto for Gem, and its Gusto board is still live), so it reads Unknown, never a zero.
Every /postings/ link must be represented, and fewer rows than cards raises: a partial read is never reported as the board.
A card stating two pay ranges, or an anchor wrapping two headings, raises rather than guess which belongs to which.

hirebridge.name: Hirebridge
hirebridge.spot: Any address on recruit., hbapi. or alerts.hirebridge.com carrying cid=<number> (find_site_boards): an iframe of the career centre (Hirebridge's stock embed, id=HBIFRAME, as on CentralSquare's careers page), a link to the classic /v3/jobs/list.aspx?cid=, a posting, or the job-alerts page. The cid is the ref; there is no name or slug in these addresses. Hint: hirebridge.com.
hirebridge.publishes: The JSON feed Hirebridge's own career centre calls from every visitor's browser, one GET for the whole board, descriptions included: https://hbapi.hirebridge.com/careercenter/v2/GetJobListings?cid=<cid>&language=en&addloc=0&startrow=1&endrow=5000. The body is a JSON string holding the JSON array, so it is decoded twice. One feed serves both UI generations (the classic list.aspx tenants and the /v3/CareerCenter/v2 ones). No paging needed: the career centre itself asks 5,000 rows a batch.
hirebridge.robots: Asked at every hop: read as pages, held to the host. Measured 2026-11-19..21: hbapi.hirebridge.com has no robots.txt (404, so no rules); recruit.hirebridge.com disallows only /application, /company, /jobseeker2 and /jobseeker4 (older career-centre forms a reader never needs).
hirebridge.employer: Stated on every row of the feed: companyname, with companyurl the website the account gave (empty on Tribute's). verify_boards._hirebridge reads the same feed, with no extra request, and holds companyurl to the website on file; rows giving two different websites are not stated. An empty feed names nobody: a cid nobody holds answers '[]' too.
quirks: THE FEED IS OVER-BROAD: each row's nested joblist carries internal requisition data (notes naming staff, hiring-manager and coordinator ids) and descriptioninternal, the ad meant for internal applicants. The reader copies the public fields by name and nothing else, and hirebridge.com is in ats.NEVER_CACHED, so no raw answer is written to disk.

An empty feed is a zero only when the classic career centre answers as a live board (titled '<Name> Career Center'); a dead cid is sent, on the same host, to /v3/Application/AppErrMsg.aspx, titled 'Hirebridge ATS Error'. Anything else is not known, and not a zero.
addloc=0 matters: without it a job open in three places comes back as three rows with one jid (EAB, 2026-11-21: 93 rows for 42 jobs).
publicdate is M/D/YYYY and read as such (posted_date refuses to guess an order); never createdate, which is when the requisition was opened.
location.isremote true means remote; false is not stated (it was false on six of the seven CentralSquare roles whose title says Remote).
The places are joblocname plus additionalLocations; neither alone is the list.
The older career-centre forms (/jobseeker2, /jobseeker4) are robots-closed: a cid lifted from such a link is read through the feed.
notes: The research said an empty feed should read as an empty board, with gone told from empty in the probe or once when the board is wired; the code's reader asks the classic career centre itself, on every empty read, and raises unless it answers as a live board. The code is what runs.

html.name: A careers page (html)
html.spot: Any careers page with no board behind it that another reader takes. Discovery also files several vendors' addresses as html (discover_ats.MARKERS): ADP's recruitment.html page, paycomonline.net's jobs?clientkey= list, jobs.jobvite.com/<slug>, <label>.teamtailor.com, applicantpro.com, clearcompany.com, isolvedhire.com, dayforcehcm.com, recruiting.ultipro.com/<TENANT>, pinpointhq.com, taleo.net, avature.net, csod.com and careers.hibob.com.
html.publishes: The page itself. refresh.py's reader, fetch_html, returns one pseudo-row carrying the page's visible text for the classifier (a page under 400 characters raises: likely JavaScript-rendered). build_board reads the same page with fetch_html_titles, which counts a link only when its address looks like a job's and its text like a title, needs two, deduplicates on the link, and takes schema.org JobPosting blocks already in the page; a shell falls back to a headless browser (render_fetch.fetch_rendered) within the nightly render budget.
html.robots: Asked at every hop (ats._page). A rendered read walks the address's redirects with ats.resolve first and keeps nothing from a page whose final address is refused.
html.employer: Names nobody: board_says' html branch records the page's own host and counts its titles ('html board: the page's own host'), and html is not in NAMES_ITS_EMPLOYER, so an html board can never pass proven().
quirks: A page scan never proves absence: an unreadable page is Unknown, never None found.
html does not mean unread: on 2026-11-18, 114 such pages put 1,357 postings on the board every night.
A page-scan verdict read off another company's careers page is downgraded to Unknown (refresh._someone_elses_site).
A commented-out job is not an opening: comments are stripped before the scan (Pantonium's three commented-out Sales Director rows had published a 'Yes').

icims.name: iCIMS
icims.spot: <slug>.icims.com (discover_ats.MARKERS, borrowed by find_site_boards; lowered), or a full portal address on icims.com. Hint: icims.com.
icims.publishes: A server-rendered portal: the plain address is a ~600-character shell with the list in an iframe, and ?in_iframe=1 returns the real list, https://<slug>.icims.com/jobs/search?ss=1&in_iframe=1&pr=<n>. Titles are the iCIMS_Anchor title attribute, '<req id> - <title>'. Paged by number (about 20 a page) until a page adds no new link, at most 60 pages, and deduplicated on the link, never the title. The ad is each posting page's schema.org JobPosting (behind FETCH_DETAILS).
icims.link: https://<slug>.icims.com/jobs/search?ss=1; a full-address ref is linked as it is.
icims.robots: Asked at every hop (ats._page). Measured 2026-10-09: iCIMS portals saying 'Disallow: /' cost Bruker Detection 213 postings and BigBear.ai 64 when the crawler began honouring robots.txt.
icims.employer: Stated on the board's own first page: iCIMS writes one sentence into the meta description, 'View all current positions at X across all categories and locations.', and X is the ACCOUNT holder (not the <title>, which employers rewrite). verify_boards._icims reads it, and a full-address ref must be on icims.com. The account can be a third party's: Selux's portal says 'Council of Industry'.
quirks: The probe reads the first page only (n_is_partial): a board's size comes from the reader, which pages to the end.
Paged to the end since 2026-09-01: Bruker's portal served nineteen on its first page and twenty after, eleven pages and 204 links; deduplicating on the title had deleted 27 real requisitions.
An empty portal raises ('no jobs parsed from iCIMS portal'): Unknown, never a zero.
A Jibe site answers ?in_iframe=1 with a script that bounces back: that is the jibe type, not this one.

jazzhr.name: JazzHR
jazzhr.spot: <slug>.applytojob.com (discover_ats.MARKERS, borrowed by find_site_boards) and the embed script app.jazz.co/widgets/basic/create/<slug> (the finder's own); lowered. Hints: applytojob.com, jazz.co.
jazzhr.publishes: A server-rendered list of <a> job links at https://<slug>.applytojob.com/apply/. The list page carries only an Organization block; the ad, and a structured baseSalary when the employer set one, are on each posting page (behind FETCH_DETAILS). No paging.
jazzhr.robots: Asked at every hop (ats._page). Not measured.
jazzhr.employer: Stated on the board's own page as a JSON-LD Organization block, with the website the employer typed beside it: verify_boards._jazzhr states the name and gives the site to proven(). An inactive board has no block and is titled 'JazzHR - Inactive Career Page', so the name is never read from the title.
quirks: A dead or mistyped slug redirects to info.jazzhr.com and on to www.jazzhr.com/job-seekers, a marketing page with an Organization block of its own (measured 2026-11-18): the probe refuses any hop off the board's host.
A page with no job links raises unless it says it has none ('no open positions' and the like): an unreadable board is not an empty one.
The title is measured after stripping: JazzHR indents its anchors by 77 characters, and a bound on the raw text kept 2 of 51 real postings (measured across twelve boards, 2026-09-01).

jibe.name: Jibe (iCIMS Talent Cloud)

An embedded board's list and postings send a browser on to the employer's own careers page; asked with nl=1&fr=false they answer themselves. A posting's own block names its job by identifier (the job's id, measured 2026-11-22 on Gigamon's postings); only the node that is this posting gives a row its ad and its pay.
A job open in several places shows only 'N Locations' on the list (Uplight's '2 Locations').
discover_ats.MARKERS still files jobs.jobvite.com/<slug> as type html.
notes: The research said build, reading the HTML list nightly and the XML feed as paced enrichment for descriptions (and Tyler's pay); the reader was built on the list alone and does not read the feed, which names hiring managers and rate-limits. The code is what runs.

The research proposed believing the title when ONE posting's JSON-LD agrees with it; the probe asks every posting, up to 40, after a blind review found one posting standing for a board (2026-11-22). The code is what runs.
The research counted Gigamon's board at 21 on 2026-11-19; the reader's own note says 22, measured 2026-11-21.

forms.pinpoint-other: An address on pinpointhq.com that names no tenant.

reporting_to names a hiring manager on some rows and is never read; the RSS body repeats it as 'Reporting To', so the ad comes from the JSON fields.
A dates feed that will not read costs the dates, never the board.

The widget form <div data-pinpoint-subdomain="<slug>"> (Democracy Works' careers page) carries no pinpointhq.com host, so the finder's markup patterns miss it; the host appears only in a rendered page's request to the feed.
discover_ats.MARKERS still files <label>.pinpointhq.com as type html.

Read from the owner's Mac (his ruling of 2026-11-17): scripts/workday_snapshot.py runs there and commits data/workday_snapshot.json, and the nightly crawl (GOVTECH_DOCK_WORKDAY_SNAPSHOT=1) takes a board from it; a board the Mac has not read in 48 hours is asked live, and a failure names the snapshot's age.

Measured 2026-11-19..21: an identical Zoho robots.txt on every tenant read allows /jobs, /jobs/ and /jobs/* and disallows everything else; the embed widget's lighter JSON (/recruit/v2/public/Job_Openings) is closed, and a live read of it was refused.
zohorecruit.employer: Stated on the page the reader reads: the meta input's org_info.company_name, with org_info.website, which proven() holds to the one on file. It is the ACCOUNT's name, so a parent's board states the parent (QuickLaunch's link goes to ElevenX Capital's). verify_boards._zohorecruit states nothing for a board set to hide its name, nor for any page but the account's default 'Careers'. Never the page title ('Jobs at Careers' on Cuseum's) nor the portal label ('exc' is ElevenX).
quirks: CLOSED JOBS ARE IN THE LIST: a row with Publish false is a job kept on view and closed (GovEase's only row, a 2025 opening), so only Publish true is read.
Every wrong address answers 200 with a page saying so, so a page without the jobs input is an error, never a zero; the input's literal [] is a zero.
On some layouts the description is a 153-character teaser ending '...' (Spektra's, ElevenX's): flagged _jd_is_teaser and never read for money.
The row has no address: the list's own address plus the id answers with the job, whatever its title becomes.
A custom domain serves the same board (careers.spektrasystems.com); the vendor's host is the one a probe can hold every read to.
notes: The research proposed the probe state org_info.company_name whenever hide_company_name is not true; the code also states nothing for any page but 'Careers', since the name is the account's and a sister brand's page would be proven for it (blind review, 2026-11-21). The code is what runs.

trakstar.name: Trakstar Hire (formerly Recruiterbox)
trakstar.why: Every tenant serves a public RSS 2.0 feed of the whole board that its own page links ('Jobs RSS Feed') and robots.txt allows: one request a company, with title, link, the full ad, pubDate and city, state and country as fields. The feed names the employer by the display name it set, which equalled the name on file on all four boards read, and a made-up slug answers a clean 404 on its own host, so a dead board cannot pass as an empty one. The payoff today is small: 4 companies, 11 postings, none of them a sales title.
trakstar.spot: Tenants live at <slug>.hire.trakstar.com; legacy <slug>.recruiterbox.com links 301 there. Nothing in the finder names either host, in BOARDS or in ELSEWHERE (a job frame from one is tallied as other:trakstar.com). trakstar.com, not recruiterbox.com, is on the vendor-host lists (build_board._PROMOTE_ATS_HOSTS, refresh._ATS_HOSTS, admin.ATS_HOSTS). Every form the research saw was a plain link: the board home, a posting with ?apply=true, a posting with ?source=. Reduce a posting link to its tenant and read the board, never the posting.
trakstar.publishes: RSS 2.0 with xmlns:job: GET https://<slug>.hire.trakstar.com/jobfeeds/<slug>, unpaged as far as measured (8 of 8 and 3 of 3 openings in one response): each item's title, link, description (the full ad as escaped HTML), pubDate, job:locationCity, job:locationState, job:locationCountry, job:positionType, job:team and job:closeDte. The board page, https://<slug>.hire.trakstar.com/, is server-rendered and gives the count (RB.init_data.total_jobs), the identity statement and the work mode in one more request.
trakstar.robots: Measured 2026-11-19..21 on four tenants (identical files): User-agent: * / Disallow: /prepare* / Disallow: /published_jobs_list_v2* / Allow: /. The board page, the RSS feed, the postings and the sitemap are allowed; /published_jobs_list_v2, the board's own list endpoint, is closed and must never be used. The legacy recruiterbox.com host serves the same file and 301s to the tenant.
trakstar.employer: Stated in the feed: <channel><title>Jobs at {Name}</title> and <description>Current open positions at {Name}</description>; also the board page's <title> and h1, and each posting's JSON-LD hiringOrganization. A pattern statement, like Gusto's 'Careers at X': a probe should take X from 'Jobs at X' and require it to equal the X in 'Current open positions at X'. An empty board's feed still states its name (Selerix). No probe is written.
quirks: Two dates that disagree: pubDate is RFC 822 at midnight +0530 (converting it to UTC moves it back a day), and a posting's JSON-LD datePosted differed from it on 4 of 9 postings compared, in both directions. Leave posted None, or take pubDate's calendar date with the owner's say-so.
Pay is free text only, with no currency stated, and 7 of RideCo's 8 roles are in Ontario, where '$' means CAD.

The feed's links are http:// with the stored client-name casing (RideCo.hire...); normalise them to https://<slug, lowered>.hire.trakstar.com/jobs/<id>/ so posting ids stay stable. The feed path ignores case, so store the slug lowered.
Posting pages' JSON-LD holds raw control characters, so ats._schema_posting (a strict json.loads) gets nothing from them.
Careers pages carry stale posting links (Focus School Software's linked posting is a 404 while its board is live).

successfactors.name: SAP SuccessFactors (Career Site Builder)
successfactors.why: Read since 2026-11-22, classic Career Site Builder boards only (ats.fetch_successfactors), built when the owner asked for Gainwell Technologies' board. Unify boards, whose list is served only by POST /services/recruiting/v1/jobs (robots-closed), are read as an error that says so, never a zero. The research (2026-11-20) rated the platform maybe: Classic Career Site Builder boards are a clean public listing: server-rendered /search/ pages on the employer's own careers host, 25 rows a page, robots-allowed, no token. Three things hold it at maybe. The newer 'Unify' search draws its results by POST /services/recruiting/v1/jobs, which every CSB robots.txt closes, leaving only sitemap.xml plus one or two requests per posting. The legacy portals companies link (careerN.successfactors.com, careerN.sapsf.com ?company=) are closed outright. And under the owner's rule only 2 of the 8 example companies would wire unattended (Landis+Gyr, and Indra Group, a 623-posting Spanish board): the rest are a parent's board, a placeholder name or a longer registered name. Worth building as a classic-CSB reader that detects Unify and reports Unknown, or falls back to the sitemap if the owner accepts the cost per posting.
successfactors.spot: A page of the company's own site that IS a classic CSB board, by its tells - assets under rmkcdn.successfactors.com/<8 hex>/, a j2w.init({... ssoCompanyId ...}) block, jQuery from an hcm<N> or performancemanager<N> (sapsf|successfactors) host, or /platform/js/j2w/ scripts - read only from the page's own scripts and attributes: the board's ref is that page's scheme and host. A link to https://<host>/go/<Name>/<digits>/ or /search/?...sortColumn=... on the company's own registrable domain gives that origin too. Never a ref from an SAP host. Legacy portals (career<N>.successfactors.(com|eu), career<N>.sapsf.(com|eu|cn), ?company=) are the vendor form successfactors-legacy: robots-closed, never a board.
successfactors.publishes: Classic: GET https://<board host>/search/?q=&sortColumn=referencedate&sortDirection=desc&startrow=<0, 25, 50, ...>, server-rendered HTML (<table id="searchresults">, one <tr class="data-row"> a posting: the jobTitle-link, jobLocation, jobDate and per-site columns), offset-paged 25 at a time with the total in the localized pagination label; category pages /go/<Name>/<catid>/<startrow>/ carry the same table. Description and pay are only on each /job/<slug>/<id>/ page. Unify: no list a reader may use; the only robots-clean list is sitemap.xml, then each posting. RSS exists under /services/rss/ and is closed. Measured on Gainwell 2026-11-22: jobs.gainwelltechnologies.com, 334 postings over 14 pages of 25, read in full in 15 requests; remote roles carry a placeholder place ('Any city, TX, US, 99999'), which the reader reads as 'TX, US'.
successfactors.robots: Measured 2026-11-19..21: a byte-identical CSB template robots.txt on all six board hosts read allows /search/, /go/, /job/ and /sitemap.xml, and disallows /services/ (the RSS and the Unify API), /talentcommunity/apply/, /applybutton/ and /preapply/. The legacy portals (career8.successfactors.com, career41.sapsf.com) serve 'Disallow: /', 'Disallow: /*company', 'Allow: /login' and were never asked.
successfactors.employer: Stated on the board's own host: the /search/ page's <title>, '{site name} Jobs', and its meta description, 'Find at {site name}' (localized: 'JENOPTIK AG - Stellen', 'Buscar en Indra Group'); classic posting pages add <meta itemprop="hiringOrganization">. The site name is whatever the admin typed: a placeholder on 2 of 6 boards ('esricanada', 'our team'), and a group's board names the parent. The ssoCompanyId in j2w.init is a tenant id, not a name. No probe is written.
quirks: Group boards name the parent and carry many units: SPX's 237 rows covered 12 units, the unit only in a site-specific 'Facility' column spelt inconsistently, where Landis+Gyr's same column holds requisition ids.

Templates are localized (en_US, de_DE and es_ES seen): the <title>, the meta description, the pagination label and the date format follow the site's default locale; pass locale=en_US where a site offers English.
Multilingual tenants list one role once per language under different ids.
A /go/ category page can carry an empty <title>: read the name from /search/.
Giants among the examples: Indra Group 623 postings (mostly Spain), SPX 237, Jenoptik 175.

forms.successfactors-legacy: A legacy Recruiting Management portal address, career<N>.successfactors.(com|eu) or career<N>.sapsf.(com|eu|cn) at /career or /careers?company=<id>: robots.txt closes it ('Disallow: /'), so it is a platform the crawl cannot read and a doubt beside a board - except on a CSB board's own pages, where it is furniture (the j2w.init ssoUrl, a sign-in link).

The old server-rendered list (jobs?clientkey=) is closed; the new career page is a JavaScript shell with no rows; its rows come from a POST to a closed host that needs a token minted into each page view; the sitemap answers 404. A reader would have to scrape a token and post to a disallowed path, which the owner's rules rule out.
paycom.spot: Any paycomonline.net or paycomonline.com address: find_site_boards tallies it as 'paycom'. Seen as an href or iframe to www.paycomonline.net/v4/ats/web.php/jobs?clientkey=<KEY> (sometimes with &fromClientSide=true), as per-posting jobs/ViewJobDetails?clientkey=<KEY>&job=<N> links, and as portal /v4/ats/web.php/portal/<KEY>/jobs/<N> links. The client key is 32 upper-case hex characters and names nobody. discover_ats.MARKERS files the old jobs?clientkey= form as type html, an address robots.txt closes, and misses the other two.
paycom.publishes: Old list: GET www.paycomonline.net/v4/ats/web.php/jobs?clientkey=<KEY> (closed). New career page: /v4/ats/web.php/portal/<KEY>/career-page, allowed, a ~235 KB shell with no rows. The rows: POST https://portal-applicant-tracking.us-cent.paycomonline.net/api/ats/job-posting-previews/search with the page's sessionJWT as its Authorization (closed, and token-gated). Open: one posting page at a time, /v4/ats/web.php/portal/<KEY>/jobs/<N>, with a schema.org JobPosting; its ids have to come from somewhere else.
paycom.robots: Measured 2026-11-19..21: both Paycom hosts serve Disallow: /, with Allow only for /v4/ats/web.php/portal/, assets, /api/ats/job-postings/, /api/ats/company-name and /api/ats/portal-settings. The old list and ViewJobDetails were refused before any request; the job-posting-previews search is refused; the allowed APIs answered 401 without the page's token; /v4/ats/sitemap.php is allowed and answered 404.
paycom.employer: Never at the board's level: the career page is titled 'Job Opportunities'. Each posting page names its employer in its JobPosting hiringOrganization.name, a payroll-style legal name in capitals ('VIMO INC', 'CODE FOUR'), one posting at a time. No probe.
quirks: A smaller job than a reader: where an employer links its postings one by one (Code Four's page does), each old ViewJobDetails?clientkey=K&job=N link can be rewritten to the allowed /v4/ats/web.php/portal/K/jobs/N, which ats._schema_posting reads unchanged. The owner should rule on that rewrite before it is built.
A posting page alone does not prove a job is open: Code Four's 2021 posting still answered 200, with no validThrough.
The discovery log marks companies retry_soon after a robots refusal of the old Paycom address; that refusal is not transient, so the retries keep failing.

render_fetch.only_allowed asks robots.txt for documents only, so a headless render of such a careers page aborts the Paycor frame and still downloads the gnewton script from the closed host (the research found it in passing; whether a subresource must ask is the owner's call).
What can be done instead: hand capture, and a posts_at ruling where a company points elsewhere.

ukg.name: UKG Pro Recruiting (UltiPro)
ukg.why: robots.txt closes the only listing by name on every UKG host measured: Disallow: */JobBoardView is longer than Allow: */JobBoard/, so the board page's own LoadSearchResults call is refused. What it leaves open carries no full list: the board page shows an employer-chosen 'featured' subset at most, and the posting pages are open but their ids come only from the closed listing. Calling it would be working around a refusal. A person can still capture roles by hand.
ukg.spot: Any ultipro.com, ultipro.ca or ukg.net address: find_site_boards tallies it as 'ukg'. ukg.publishes: The listing is the board page's own background call, POST https://<host>/<TENANT>/JobBoard/<uuid>/JobBoardView/LoadSearchResults (pageSize 50, paged by skip with a totalCount, per the page's markup; never called). The board page (437 KB to 3.5 MB) carries only a featured subset, filter facets and the tenant's job-title catalog; a posting page (OpportunityDetail?opportunityId=<id>) is open and fully structured. ukg.robots: Measured 2026-11-19..21 on recruiting.ultipro.com, recruiting2.ultipro.com, recruiting.ultipro.ca and bellhowell.rec.pro.ukg.net: the same 144-character file, User-agent: * / Disallow: / / Allow: */JobBoard/ / Disallow: */JobBoardView / Disallow: */JobBoard/*/Styles / Disallow: */JobBoard/*/AnonymousSessionCheck. The listing and its filter, count and typeahead calls are refused; the board page and OpportunityDetail are allowed; the tenant root is refused.

It equalled the company's name on 2 of 7 boards (i3 Verticals, Bell and Howell); the others read like 'Honorlock Opportunities' and 'Neptune Careers'. There is no company field anywhere, and tenant aliases are codes. No probe.
quirks: A board uuid that does not exist under a real tenant redirects to that tenant's board instead of failing, so a reader would have to check it landed on the uuid it asked.
Parent tenants: Muni-Link's careers page links Neptune's board on Roper's tenant.
A reader that took only the featured rows would mislead: 5 of 7 boards feature nothing, and an empty featured list proves nothing.
welcome-us.ukg.net/u/login is UKG's employee sign-in, not a board, and the finder counts any ukg.net link as 'ukg'.
